## What is on the page

Round is a made-up bill-splitting app. The page is built so a visitor uses the product before reading about it.

| Section | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Loading sequence | A white ring draws itself while the bill adds up, flies into the hero and peels into one slice per person. |
| Hero | The ring is live. Drag a line to move money between two people, tap a face to add or drop someone, set the tip. Every figure rolls to its new value. |
| Statement and bill | A sentence inks in word by word as you scroll. Then a bill where tapping a face moves an item on or off that person, with four bills to try. |
| Settle | One pinned screen. The scroll drives an odometer the width of the screen and ticks off each debt as the figure passes it. |
| Numbers and quotes | Three figures that roll in when they come into view, and three quotes. |
| Pricing and questions | Monthly or yearly prices, then five questions. |
| Last call and footer | The closing line, two buttons and the footer. |

The switch in the top bar changes the currency of every figure on the page at once.

## Install

```npm
npx shadcn@latest add @keyframery/round
```

That copies the page into `components/round/`, installs the five Keyframery components it uses and adds the `motion` package. Then render it on a route:

```tsx title="app/page.tsx"
import { RoundLanding } from "@/components/round/round"

export default function Page() {
  return <RoundLanding />
}
```

To have a coding agent do it, and then rewrite it for your product, use **Copy for your coding agent** at the top of this page and paste the result into Claude Code, Cursor or Codex.

## Make it yours

- **Words, people, bills and prices** are all in `data.ts`. The sections read from that file and nothing else.
- **Colours** are six values at the top of `round.css`: blue, ink, paper, hot, pink and sky. Each section picks a tone with `data-tone`, and the controls inside it follow.
- **Photos** load from keyframery.com after an install. Replace the paths in `data.ts` with your own.
- **Motion** follows the [motion style](/docs/motion-styles) of your site. It is quiet by default; set `data-motion="springy"`, `"calm"`, `"snappy"` or `"playful"` on `<html>` and the whole page changes pace.

## How it is built

- **Controls** are UI SDK components through Keyframery: the tip is a [Slider](/docs/components/slider), the faces are [Toggles](/docs/components/toggle), the currency and billing switches are [Segmented Controls](/docs/components/segmented-control), the questions are an [Accordion](/docs/components/accordion) and every button is a [Button](/docs/components/button). Keyboard and screen-reader behaviour come from UI SDK.
- **Motion** is in two parts. [Motion](https://motion.dev) drives what needs real springs and the scroll: the ring flying into place, the odometer, the statement, content swapping in the bill and the buttons that lean toward the pointer. Everything else is plain CSS.
- **Reduced motion** skips the loading sequence and stops every transition. The page stays fully usable.
- **Phone to desktop.** The layout is designed at 390px and at 1440px, not scaled between them.
